                                 REGULAR MEETING MINUTES

                  BOARD OF RECREATION AND PARKS COMMISSIONERS
                            OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES

                                 Thursday September 17, 2026

The Board of Recreation and Park Commissioners of the City of Los Angeles convened the Regular
Meeting at 9:32 a.m. Present were, Vice President Tafarai Bayne, Commissioner Marie Lloyd, and
Commissioner Mary Rosas. Also present were, Jimmy Kim, General Manager, Matthew Rudnick,
Executive Officer, Deputy City Attorney IV Steven Hong and Deputy City Attorney III Brendan
Kearns.


The following Department staff members were also present:

Cathie Santo Domingo, Superintendent Planning Maintenance, and Construction Branch
Chinyere Stoneham, Assistant General Manager, Recreation Services Branch
Brenda Aguirre, Assistant General Manager, Special Operations Branch
John Busby, Sr. Management Analyst, Finance Administration Branch

CALL TO ORDER


APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES

President Sanchez called for a motion to approve the minutes of the Regular Meeting of
September 3, 2026. Vice President Bayne made such motion, and it was seconded by
Commissioner Rosas. There being no objections, the motion was unanimously approved by a
vote of 3-0.

Commissioner Chase joined the meeting at 9:45 and Commissioner Lloyd joined the meeting at
9:48.


GENERAL MANAGER’S UPDATE

Jimmy Kim, General Manager began his update by introducing Sonya Young-Jimenez , the
Superintendent of the West Region Recreation Branch to provide an overview of the facility and
to introduce the staff at the Penmar Recreation Center.

Mr. Kim mentioned that the Commission Office has received various communications from
constituents, and we have assigned appropriate staff for follow-up. Mr. Kim began with updates
that were requested by the Commissioners at a previous meeting. Mr. Kim provided an update on
this past summer's swimming pool operations, as well as splash pad operation. Out of the 15
splash pads, 2 splash pads were in operational. St. Andrews and Mason splash pads. The St.
Andrews Splash Pad did not meet the LA County Health and Safety Recreational water
standards for safe overturn of the water filtration. And that was because when it was designed,
they didn't think it was going to be used as much as it's been used. And so, the filter is currently
undersized and not suitable for the application, and the circulation pump. For Mason RC,

                                                 1
similarly, same type of issue. It was a matter of the system continuing to fail because the filters
just simply cannot keep up with the load of the users. So, we're looking at both locations, to
identify funding to get those repaired and hopefully replaced and up and running before next
summer. In terms of our swimming pools, out of our 52 total swimming pools across our park
system. This past summer, we had 3 pools that did not open. Due to, whether it's a mechanical
failure or through just not passing health and safety codes. Those three parks were Griffith Park
Pool, Costello and Peck Pool Park.

Mr. Kim mentioned RAP is preparing for El Nino and significant rain through coordinated facility
assessments, preventative maintenance, emergency staffing, and evacuation center readiness.
As you all know, this department is also tasked as a secondary role that we take very seriously in
mass care and, public welfare, in times of local disaster.



GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENTS


Public comments on matters within the Board's jurisdiction were invited, 22 such requests were
submitted.

BOARD REPORT PUBLIC COMMENT AND CONSIDERATION OF THE BOARD REPORTS

Public comments relevant to the Board Reports were requested; 22 such requests were submitted.

NEIGHBORHOOD COUNCIL COMMENTS

Discussion with Neighborhood Council Representatives on Neighborhood Council Resolutions or
Community Impact Statements Filed with the City Clerk Relative to Any Item Listed or Being
Considered on this Board of Recreation and Park Commissioners Meeting Agenda (Los Angeles
Administrative Code 22.819; Ordinance 184243)

There was no such comment from Neighborhood Council Representatives relative to the Agenda
Items being considered.

President Sanchez requested a Motion to approve the Board Reports that were taken on Consent
26-207, 26-208, 26-209, 26-211, 26-212, 26-213, 26-214 and 26-215. It was moved by
Commissioner Rosas and seconded by Commissioner Chase. There being no objections, the
motion was unanimously approved by a vote of 5-0.

President Sanchez requested a Motion to approve Board Report 26-216, and 26-217 as
presented It was moved by Commissioner Chase and seconded by Vice President
Bayne. There being no objections, the motion was unanimously approved by a vote of 5-0.


COMMISSION TASK FORCE UPDATES

Commission Task Force on Concessions

Commissioner Rosa stated this task force has not met.

Commission Task Force on Facility Repair and Maintenance

                                                5
Commissioner Lloyd stated this task force met and discussed, an Echo Park Art Project, which
will be installed in the pool room. She mentioned we also went over a stormwater project in
Wilmington. Commissioner Lloyd also stated the task force discussed the South Griffith Park
Master Plan.

COMMISSION BUSINESS


Comments from the Commissioners on Matters within the Board’s jurisdiction and Requests by
Commissioners to Schedule Specific Future Agenda Items were requested. Vice President
Bayne requested a report back on internal turf policies Commissioner Lloyd and Commissioner
Chase both requested more detailed information when it comes to artificial turf verses natural
grass. Commissioner Chase requested more information on the Penmar and Rancho
Concessions. Commissioner Chase also requested more information on the Carousel at
Centennial Park. Commissioner Lloyd would like to see how the Parks Needs Assessment is
infiltrating the way that we structure our staff, our priorities, our budgets. I've asked for, at a basic
level, to have it be a part of our board reports.




ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business to come before the Board, the Meeting adjourned at 11:24 a.m.
